events.title: Potsdam Conference Begins
events.description: Leaders of the United States, United Kingdom, and Soviet Union (Truman, Churchill, and Stalin) convened in Potsdam, Germany, to negotiate the terms of post-World War II Europe, including the administration of defeated Germany and the reorganization of borders.
events.significance: The conference shaped the postwar order in Europe, formalized the division of Germany into occupation zones, and highlighted growing tensions that would lead to the Cold War.

events.title: Disneyland Opens in Anaheim, California
events.description: Walt Disney's Disneyland theme park held its opening day ceremony, with a televised event that was marred by heat, overcrowding, and counterfeit tickets, but it opened to the public the next day.
events.significance: Disneyland became the model for modern theme parks worldwide and transformed the global entertainment and tourism industries.

events.title: Execution of the Romanov Family
events.description: Tsar Nicholas II, his wife Alexandra, and their five children were executed by Bolshevik forces in the early hours of July 17 (some accounts say the night of July 16-17) in Yekaterinburg, Russia.
events.significance: The killings ended the Romanov dynasty, which had ruled Russia for over 300 years, and marked a defining moment of the Russian Civil War.

events.title: Apollo-Soyuz Test Project Docking
events.description: An American Apollo spacecraft and a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft docked in orbit, and the crews shared a historic handshake in space.
events.significance: It was the first international crewed space mission and a symbol of détente between the United States and the Soviet Union during the Cold War.

events.title: Rome Statute Adopted
events.description: Delegates from 120 nations voted to adopt the Rome Statute, establishing the International Criminal Court to prosecute genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity.
events.significance: The treaty created the first permanent international criminal court, advancing global accountability for the gravest crimes.
